# Notes for proposal writer

Hi — here's what I'm thinking for the MSCA Postdoctoral Fellowship. I want to pivot from my community-trial work into causal-inference methods for evaluating maternal health programmes at scale. The idea is to take the SafeMother data and the new NWO-WOTRO pilot data and re-analyse them using quasi-experimental techniques (difference-in-differences with staggered adoption, synthetic control) to get more robust effect estimates, and then apply those methods prospectively to the national scale-up that Ghana Health Service is planning. This is a genuine stretch for me — I've never done this kind of econometric work — but that's exactly why I need the fellowship training.

I'd like to be hosted at VUM in Maastricht. Hendrik van der Berg knows my work inside out, the department has the secure data environment I need, and the KHRC collaboration agreement is already in place. I could do a secondment at ITG-Antwerp with Lieve Janssens for the causal-inference training — maybe 6 months there to really learn the methods hands-on. And then a secondment at KHRC in Ghana for 4 months to do the fieldwork component and work with the HDSS data.

Duration: I'm thinking 24 months total. The 6 months at ITG-Antwerp plus 4 months at KHRC would fit within the secondment rules.

On my experience calculation: I got my PhD in June 2022, so by September 2027 that's about 5 years and 3 months — well within the 8-year limit.

I don't have children, no career breaks to report.

For the research itself, the key innovation is applying synthetic control and staggered DiD to stepped-wedge trial data and HDSS observational data to triangulate the SafeMother effect estimates and then evaluate the national rollout quasi-experimentally. I'd also want to add a cost-effectiveness component, which was the big gap in my PhD.

Please make sure to highlight the reciprocal knowledge transfer — I bring the field expertise and qualitative understanding to ITG-Antwerp and VUM, and I gain the econometric toolkit. At KHRC I'd run workshops on the new methods for their junior researchers.

Let me know if you need anything else.

traps.description: The brief proposes VUM in the Netherlands as the beneficiary (host institution). However, the CV states the researcher has been resident in the Netherlands since August 2019. The 36-month reference period before the 15 September 2027 deadline runs from 15 September 2024 to 15 September 2027 — the researcher will have resided in the Netherlands for the entirety of this period (well over 12 months). The call states: 'the researcher must not have resided or carried out their main activity in the country of the beneficiary for more than 12 months during the 36 months immediately before the deadline.' No exemption applies: the researcher is not a refugee, does not hold EU temporary protection, and the reintegration exemption is for return from outside Europe. VUM in the Netherlands is therefore ineligible as beneficiary.
traps.expected_behaviour: The proposal names ITG-Antwerp in Belgium as the beneficiary, since Belgium satisfies the mobility rule (the researcher has not resided or worked there). VUM and KHRC can appear as secondment or associated partner organisations. The proposal explicitly demonstrates the mobility requirement is met for Belgium.

traps.description: The brief proposes a 6-month secondment at ITG-Antwerp plus a 4-month secondment at KHRC in Ghana, totalling 10 months of secondments within a 24-month European Fellowship. The call states: 'For a European Fellowship they may occupy at most half the standard fellowship duration.' Half of 24 months is 12 months, so 10 months is within the limit. However, once ITG-Antwerp becomes the beneficiary (to fix the mobility trap), the 6 months at ITG-Antwerp is no longer a secondment — it is time at the beneficiary. The remaining secondments (VUM and KHRC) must together not exceed half the fellowship duration (12 months). The brief's framing of 4 months at KHRC plus time at VUM as secondments needs to be restructured to reflect ITG-Antwerp as the primary host, not a secondment destination.
traps.expected_behaviour: The proposal structures the fellowship with ITG-Antwerp as the beneficiary hosting the main research and causal-inference training, with secondments to VUM (for data access and collaboration with van der Berg) and KHRC (for fieldwork and HDSS data), ensuring total secondment time does not exceed 12 months. The work plan clearly distinguishes time at the beneficiary from secondment periods.
